release_notes: Fix the macOS bug where the app stopped receiving Ready alerts overnight and had to be restarted every morning. The peer list kept showing the office's stations as online (LanDiscovery uses UDP, which survives macOS sleep/wake cleanly), but no incoming Ready alerts reached the log or played a sound. Root cause: MessageServer's accept() loop exited on the first OSError after wake — and macOS routinely returns OSError from accept() on a TCP listening socket that lived through a sleep cycle, with no in-kernel recovery. Pre-1.0.60 the server thread just terminated and no incoming TCP connection could be accepted until the user quit and reopened the app. Outgoing Ready alerts and UDP discovery were unaffected, which is why the office looked healthy until someone tried to ping the Mac. Two layered fixes: (1) MessageServer._run_server now wraps bind/listen/accept in an outer 'while running' loop, so a failed accept() closes the dead socket and re-binds on the same port instead of exiting the thread — this is the always-on safety net for any future socket-level failure, not just sleep/wake. (2) The macOS app delegate now subscribes to NSWorkspaceDidWakeNotification and proactively bounces stop_network()+start_network() on wake, rebuilding the listener and shaking loose any half-dead inbound recv loops before the user notices anything is wrong. Windows is unaffected (desktops usually don't sleep, and the Store build's tray autostart path keeps the process running across user-session changes); the fix only changes behavior on Macs that sleep. No new dependencies; the PyObjC modules used by the wake observer are the same ones already required by the macOS tray icon and Dock-reopen handler.
